messages.author: 2430f2828c808219
messages.subject: beta-binomial distribution (documentation typo?)
parts:
Hi all

On page 280 of the latest manual the following is stated:
n ~ beta_binomial(N,alpha);
Increment log probability with beta_binomial_log(n,N,alpha), dropping
constant additive terms; Section 23.3 explains sampling statements.

But isn't there supposed to be a third argument here, i.e. beta, as shown later with the beta_binomial_log function?

Thanks,
Andrew

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] beta-binomial distribution (documentation typo?)
parts:
Hi Andrew,

No, there's no typo. If you look in Section 23.3, it explains that Stan takes:
  n ~ beta_binomial(N, alpha);

as a notational convenience for:
  increment_log_prob(beta_binomial_log(n, N, alpha));

The function beta_binomial_log has 3 arguments, the first is the left hand side of the sampling statement.



Daniel

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] beta-binomial distribution (documentation typo?)
parts:
What has happened to "beta"?...  The beta_binomial_log function has *4* arguments in my manual not 3:
real beta_binomial_log(ints n, ints N, reals alpha, reals beta)
The log beta-binomial probability mass of n successes in N trials given prior
success count (plus one) of alpha and prior failure count (plus one) of beta

Andrew
